messages:
alex chen: Quick flag — CI perf bot tripped on a throughput regression for the bf16 model family when serving at seq_len 128 on our SM92 test pool. Throughput down ~18% vs baseline. suspects: kernel pick + seqlen gating.
kevin nguyen: ugh. is this the same fallback we've seen where tensorcore path isn't picked because the capability flag is missing from the driver probe?
sara liu: can you paste the perf output from the test run? small threads like this are usually the heuristics voting wrong (seqlen threshold flips at 96/128)
alex chen: pasted below — this is the CI profile from yesterday (annotated). note the kernel chosen is matmul_fallback_sm86 not tc_bf16_sm92.

```text
# CI run: smoke/long-throughput
node: sm92-rt-7
model: llama-bf16-7b
seq_len: 128
batch: 8
chosen_kernel: matmul_fallback_sm86
throughput_tok/s: 12.2k  # baseline 14.9k
latency_p95: 312ms
kv_cache_hit_ratio: 0.92
probe_flags: sm_version=92, tensor_cores=false, bf16=true, fp8=false
```

jitendra patel: interesting — probe_flags shows tensor_cores=false. but hardware should expose TC on sm92. maybe driver quirk with that kernel microcode. did the probe run the tensorcore microbench?alex chen: CI probe only checks sm_version and bitflags from driver, not a quick microbench. we have seen drivers that report incomplete capability bits on older kernels.
kevin nguyen: two levers: 1) make the probe run a tiny tensorcore microbench during node init (fast) and set tensor_cores=true if passes, or 2) change kernel heuristic to prefer tc path when bf16+sm>=90 and fallback to microbench only on mismatch.
sara liu: also check seqlen gating hysteresis — our heuristic flips kernel at exactly 120 tokens in code. if kv cache is cold or batch shapes vary, it might flip mid-run and thrash caches.

perfbot: perfbot summary: autotune_sweep detected discrepancy: expected kernel tc_bf16_sm92, actual matmul_fallback_sm86. measured -17.9% throughput, +8% tail latency. Recommendation: run quick tc microbench on a sample of nodes and/or bump seqlen hysteresis to 16 tokens.

alex chen: Plan proposal —
- short term: add microbench probe to node bootstrap that runs a tiny bf16/tc GEMM (5ms) and sets capability flag (rollout to canary pool).  (owner: kevin)
- medium term: adjust heuristic: require seqlen > 136 for automatic tc path, add hysteresis window +-16, and record decisions to trace logs. (owner: sara)
- follow-up: audit existing node inventory for mismatched probe flags and backfill via remote job. (owner: jitendra)

kevin nguyen: i'll implement the microbench as an opt-in canary flag first. microbench pseudocode:

```bash
# run during node init (non-blocking to workloads)
/opt/redwood/bin/tc_probe --size 256 --iters 20 --dtype bf16 --threshold 0.9 || echo "no-tc"
```

if pass then set runtime.cap_flags.tensor_cores = true in node metadata.
sara liu: for heuristic changes i'll open a PR with the seqlen hysteresis impl and add an event in the decision path like `kernel_pick(reason=seqlen_hysteresis, score=...)` so Console and traces can show why a kernel was chosen.
jitendra patel: for KV interactions — the trace shows kv_cache warmup at ~3 tokens for this model but the kernel switch happens before stable cache behavior. suggest delaying kernel switch until kv_cache_hits > 0.8 for two consecutive requests.

alex chen: +1 to all. let's run a 24h canary with the probe patch on 10% of sm92 pool and compare CI smoke runs. if throughput returns to baseline we can ship.
kevin nguyen: starting a canary rollout now (tag: tc-probe-canary). will post results in this thread.

perfbot: canary kickoff: 10% sm92 nodes, tag=tc-probe-canary, started=1778004350, expected-check=1778090750
sara liu: tiny nit — log key should be `kernel_pick.source` not `kernel_pick.reason` to match existing observability schema.

alex chen: noted. i'll track that in the PR review. thanks all :thumbsup:
kevin nguyen: update — initial microbench pass on 3/3 canary nodes, setting tensor_cores=true. re-running CI workload now.
perfbot: canary perf snapshot (interim): nodes=3, avg_throughput +15.4%, p95 -6.2% (vs baseline), timestamp=1778004408
alex chen: excellent. keeping this open until we have 24h run.
kevin nguyen: filed an issue to follow-up on older driver kernels that may never report TC bits (we'll need vendor docs). issue #3109
sara liu: i'll draft the heuristic PR tomorrow and link here.
jitendra patel: i'll schedule the inventory backfill job next week.
alex chen: resolving for now but keeping thread for canary updates. thanks everyone!
